data.revised_prompt:
Create a single horizontal sprite strip for a digital pet in a clean pixel-art sprite style, using the attached reference/base pet as the canonical identity. Output exactly 6 separate animation frames arranged left-to-right in one row, evenly spaced, each frame centered within its slot, with safe padding around the character. Use the attached layout guide only as a guide for frame count, slot spacing, centering, and padding. Background should be transparent or a solid chroma-magenta placeholder only if transparency is not possible.

Subject identity lock: preserve the exact same pet design across all frames: a compact observability guardian rabbit, warm brown and cream palette, sturdy chibi silhouette, thick dark outline, small floppy ears, calm focused eyes, tiny service badge on the chest, reliable engineer energy. Keep head shape, ear shape, limb shape, face design, markings, palette, outline weight, body proportions, prop/accessory placement, and overall silhouette consistent with the canonical base pet. Do not redesign or mutate the character. Only vary pose/action for an idle animation.

Animation direction: subtle idle cycle, readable but restrained, with gentle micro-movements only. Make each frame distinct: slight breathing, tiny ear bounce, minimal head bob, tiny paw shift, subtle torso rise/fall, slight blink progression in one or two frames, and a small tail or body sway if it exists in the base design. Keep the pose grounded and calm. Do not change costume, badge, facial identity, or proportions. Use Codex digital pet sprite style, simplified from any high-resolution reference details. Ensure consistent scale and framing across all 6 frames.
